title: # 14 The Battle Of Yarmook & Abu Bakr’s Death
arabic:
اَعُوْذُ بِاللهِ مِنَّ الشِّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيْمِ۝بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَانِ الرَّحِيْمَ۝

اَلْحَمْدُ لله ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلى سَيِّدِنَا محمد وَعَلَى اَلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ تَسْلِيْمًا كَثِيْرا أبشروا وقلما جاء محصور بخير

وَالْعَصْرِ ۝ إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ۝

إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ ۝ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ۝

آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ۝

وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ۝

وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ۝

هذا يومٌ من أيَّام الله أنت سيفٌ مِنْ سُيوفِ اللهِ،  سَلَّهُ اللهُ على المشركين إِنَّمَا أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِى ۚ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُول الله

أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُول الله يَا نصرالله أقترب ، يَا نصرالله أقترب وقلما ياتي بمحصور بخير

ألبيعة ألموت، تبابعنا على الموت وليس فينا مِثلَ اللهمَّ أعْلم ألخير بعدك وكُنْتُ ألْزَمُ رَسولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عليه وسلَّمَ علَى مِلْءِ بَطْنِي،

أجلِسُونِي "أمَّرتُ عليهم ألقويُّ الأمين" إِنَّمَا أَنَا مُتَّبِعٌ وَلَسْتُ بِمُبْتَدِعٍ تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ رحم الله أبا بكر، لقد أتعب من بعده

صَّلَواةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلى سَيِّدِ ألأولين والآخرين محمد إبن عبدالله وَعلى اَلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك نشهد و الله إله إلَّا أنت نستغفرك ونتوب عليك

اَعُوْذُ بِاللهِ مِنَّ الشِّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيْمِ۝بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَانِ الرَّحِيْمَ۝

اَلْحَمْدُ لله ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلى سَيِّدِنَا محمد وَعَلَى اَلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلِّمْ تَسْلِيْمًا كَثِيْرا أبشروا فقلما جاء محصور بخير

وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ۝

هذا يومٌ من أيَّام الله أنت سيفٌ مِنْ سُيوفِ اللهِ، سَلَّهُ اللهُ على المشركين إِنَّمَا أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِى ۚ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُول الله

أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُول الله يَا نصرالله أقترب، يَا نصرالله أقترب وقلما حياتي بمحصور بخير

ألبيعة ألموت، تبابعنا على الموت عملية الأستشهادية حضرت سعید بن زید بن نفیلؓ اورحضرت سعد ابن ابی وقاصؓ ولیس فینا مِثلَ وكُنْتُ ألْزَمُ رَسولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَى مِلْءِ بَطْنِي،

أجلِسُونِي "أمَّرتُ عليهم ألقويُّ الأمين" إِنَّمَا أَنَا مُتَّبِعٌ وَلَسْتُ بِمُبْتَدِعٍ تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ رحم الله أبا بكر، لقد أتعب من بعده

english:
The Muslims assembled their army of 40 to 45,000 soldiers while, their opponent was about 250,000.

And Heraclius has chosen the battlefield, by sending a letter to his brother Theodore, who was the head of his armies.

He said: Choose a place that offers a lot of space for fighting, but very narrow for retreat.

Because he wanted to force his soldiers into fighting, they've already experienced fighting the Muslims, in a few incidents before.

You have the Battle of Mu'ta(مؤته) and then Ajnadeen(أجنادين) that just happened before Al-Yarmook(يرموك).

The one, we talked about last time.

In which Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) went to rescue Amr Bin Al-Aas(عَمْرُو بِن اَلْعَاص) in Falastine(فلسطين) and they routed the Roman army and it was disastrous defeat for the Roman emperor.

So now he assembled a huge army and he told his brother, Theodore, to make sure that there's no place to retreat.

So we can force our soldiers to fight.

So in addition to them, having their backs towards the cliff, overlooking the valley of Al-Yarmook(أليرموك), they also had the infantry, the soldiers, every 10 were tied to each other in chains.

So every group of 10 soldiers had a chain, binding them together, so that if somebody wants to run away, he has to convince the whole group.

Plus it makes it very difficult for them to move, therefore, it's almost a fixed position.

Not all of the infantry were like that, but such a huge number of them were chained.

And that was, I mean, not the first time this method was employed, because in the Battle of Dat-As-Salasal(ذات ألسلاسل), the same thing happened with Amr Bin Al-Aas رضي الله عنه,

so this was a method employed actually to force these soldiers to fight.

So now, it was Romans who chose this battlefield and when Amr Bin Al-Aas(عَمْرُو بِن اَلْعَاص), he saw that he said to the Muslims; Rejoice for the good news because rarely does a person, who's cornered, win.

They are the ones, who chose to corner themselves into this position.

So this is the beginning of the good news, that's a good omen for us.

The Roman army was divided into squadrons that was their method in fighting.

While it wasn't a tradition in Arabia to use that method, but the first time it was used was in Al-Yarmook(يرموك).

And it was the suggestion of Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه to use it.

So, he divided the army into squadrons, each squad was made up of 1000 soldiers, so he had between 40 to 45 squadrons in the army, and he would appoint a leader over each of these groups.

The heart or the center was made up of about 18 squadrons, so we're talking about 18,000 and was headed by Abu Obaidah Amr Bin Jarrah(أبوعبيدةعمروبن جرَّاح).

The right flank 10 squadrons we're talking about 10,000 and this was headed by Amr Bin Al-Aas(عَمْرُو بِن اَلْعَاص) and Sharhabil Bin Hasana(شرحبيل بن حسنة) was assisting him.

And the left flank 10 squadrons and it was headed by Yazeed Ibn Abi Sufiyan(يزيدإبن أبي سفيان).

In the front Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) placed a very small group of cavalry that could be very fast in maneuvering and would not be very restricted in their movement.

He placed them in the front and then in the rear, he placed 5000 soldiers under the leadership of Saeed Bin Zaid(سعيد بن زيد).

And the role of this group of 5000 was to defend and take care of the Muslim families and their property.

See with all of these Mujahideen(مجاهدين) they came in with their families and their wealth, their property, everything, Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله).

And you can't just leave them somewhere without protection.

So they had to accompany the army in order to be close to the protection.

So it was a very risky business don't think that for the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم and the ones, who joined them, it was an easy thing.

I mean, you just enlist in the army and go and fight for six months and then you're back, it was such a sacrifice.

Now not all of them would take their families with them, but the ones who came from very distance and faraway lands, they will bring in their families and they will just settle in that land.

And many of these fighters when Ash-Sham(ألشَّام) was opened, they did not go back to their original lands, they stayed there.

And they inhabited those areas and they spread on the religion and they made Da'wah(دعوة), so their whole life was given to Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ, it was fighting and Da'wah(دعوة).

Ad-Da'wah Wal-Jihad(ألدعوة والجهاد), that's how they lived.

So this was the formation of the Muslim army and Abu Dardah رضي الله عنه was appointed Qazi(قاضي), the judge for the army, if you get into disputes and problems.

So the army has to have a judge, and that was a Abu Dardah(أبودرداء).

Abdullah Bin Masood(عبدالله بن مسعود), he was the paymaster, he was dealing with the finances of the army.

Al-Miqdad Bin Amr Bin Aswad(ألمقداد إبن عمرو بن أسود), he was the Qari(قاري) for the army.

This was something started by Rasool Allah ﷺ in the Battle of Badr(بدر).

Rasool Allah ﷺ appointed Al-Miqdad(ألمقداد) to go around the army reciting the Surah(سورة) of Jihad(جهاد), which is Al-Anfal(ألأنفال).

So he would go around reciting the Ayaat(آيات) from Surat-Ul-Anfaal(سورة الأنفال) to the army.

And this tradition was carried on and was employed in the Battle of Yarmook(يرموك) and Khalid(خالد) appointed the same person to do it, Miqdad Ibn Aswad(ألمقداد إبن أسود), who did it in the Battle of Badr(بدر) with Rasool Allah ﷺ.

And then there was the motivator for the army, Al-Waiz(ألوائظ).

The one who would go around, encouraging the soldiers because Shaytan(شَيْطَانْ) is gonna come to you.

And he's gonna remind you about your family and he's gonna remind you about your wealth and he's gonna throw all of this Waswasah(وسوسة) in your heart.

So there needs to be somebody who's going to give you Naseeha(نَصيحة).

See in Surat-Ul-Asr(سورة العصر) Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ tells us the solution to the state of lost that every man is in.

In the name of time! Man is in a state of loss, Except for those, who believe, They do good, And they support and advise each other in Haqq(حَقّ) and Sabr(صبر), in the truth,

they advise each other to follow Al-Haqq(ألحَقّ), which is Islam, the truth and Sabr(صبر), they encourage each other to be patient.

So when you see me weak, you uplift me.

And when I see you weak, I would do the same. This is the, They would encourage each other to be patient, the one who would do that for the army was Abu Sufiyan Ibn Harb(أبوسفيان إبن حرب).

And this is the power of Islam.

Abu Sufiyan(أبوسُفيان), who was the leader of the effort to fight Muhammadﷺ, all the way until close to the death of Muhammadﷺ he turns around and he himself becomes a Muslim.

Not only does he become a Muslim, but a very enthusiastic one.

Turns around and now the one, who was motivating and mobilizing all of the tribes to fight Muhammadﷺ he is now the one encouraging them to fight the enemies of Muhammadﷺ.

So Abu Sufiyan(أبوسُفيان), he would go and speak to each Squadron and give them Mu'aza(مؤعظة).

And he would then go to the women and give them Mu'aza(مؤعظة) too because the women had a very important role to play.

They were not just sitting in the tents, to be defended by the men the women were responsible for the services of the Army, in addition to their role in fighting too.

And in the Battle of Yarmook(يرموك), the women did participate in fighting and we'll get to that and the reason, why they had to fight.

And the general commander is Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) invented this or employed this method of dividing the army into squadrons because it's a large army.

So far the Muslims have never had an army that's 40,000 strong.

It was much smaller numbers, therefore, you didn't need to split the army in this way.

In the Battle of Badr(بدر) it was 300, a little over 300.

They didn't have to be split.

Rasool Allah ﷺ the formation that he used was center, right and left that's it.

And this carried on and in many of the battles because of their method of fighting, which is the raiding method of attacking and then retreating,

you can't have that strict formation.

But now since it's a large army, it has to be more organized.

So he divided it into these squadrons.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), he told the army, he gave them a Khut'ba(خطبة), a speech and he said; This is a day from amongst the days of Allah.

See, everyday belongs to Allah but when he says this is the day of the days of Allah, he means that this is a special day.

These battles were decisive moments in history.

Many of them only took one day.

The Battle of Badr(بدر) was one day, Uhud(أحَد) was one day.

Fathh-Makkah(فتح مكَّه) was one day.

But these were life changing events for the Muslim community and they change the coarse of history.

So Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), before the battle, he is telling them, this is a day of the days of Allah.

There should be in it neither pride nor wrongdoing, throw away all of the pride because now Khalid(خالد) is dealing with different people, from different backgrounds, from different tribes.

So there's a lot of room for competition and pride and showing off who's stronger.

So Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) is saying: Throw all of that away, leave it behind you.

And it's not the day of wrongdoing.

Every day we're supposed to stay away from sins, but this is a special day.

So there's an added emphasis; be careful, on this day be closer to Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ than usual.

Make your striving sincere, Ikhlaas(إخلاص), he is giving them the Naseeha(نَصيحة) of Ikhlaas(إخلاص), which is very important in every Ibadah(عبادة), especially in their Ibadah(عبادة) of Jihad(جهاد)

because you might die the next moment.

So you have to have Ikhlaas(إخلاص).

Seeking Allah by your work for this day also has what lies beyond it.

And then Abu Sufiyan(أبوسُفيان) would go around encouraging the army.

Bahaan(بحان), one of the leaders of the Romans.

He wanted to meet with Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), so he came ahead and he asked for Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) to come and meet him.

So they met each other.

Bahaan(بحان) said: We heard that you came out in search of booty because you are very hungry and destitute people.

So I'm offering you 10 Dinar(دينار) each for every soldier in addition to a set of clothes, and food and next year, we'll give you the same.

Now, first of all, that was the reputation of the tribes of Arabia, that their life is based on raiding others.

Number two, many people cannot understand the motivation behind Jihad(جهاد) Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله).

They don't comprehend it and until this day, they don't understand it.

They fail to see that, it is for the sake of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ a person who's dying is dying for the sake of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ for something greater, for Jannah(جنة), to please Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

Somebody whose thinking is limited to this world, and cannot go beyond that doesn't understand this concept.

Why are you throwing yourself in this danger, why are you killing yourself?

How came you are doing that?

So he's saying that if you're here for money, I'm going to give you money.

Go back to your land!

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and Allah Alam(الله أعلم), how come Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) responded in this way?

Maybe he felt because the man is being, sarcastic I don't want to say sarcastic but maybe he's belittling the Muslims by such a statement.

But Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), he said: No, that's not why we came.

We came because we are people, who drink blood!

And we heard that the best tasting blood is the blood of the Romans.

So obviously, that's not an answer that Bahaan(بحان) liked.

Bahaan(بحان) said: Well, we heard that about you.

Not in that sense, but in the sense that you are very ruthless people.

And that was the reputation of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد).

See Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), a legend was developing around them.

Some of it is true, and some of it is false.

Because later on when the battle started, a man who's mentioned in At-Tabari(ألطبري) as Gerja(جرجه), which most likely he is George.

You know, an Arabic sometimes the non Arabic names, when they're converted to Arabic would sound very different.

So he tried to find what is the closest Latin name to it, because these were Latin names.

So most likely Gerja(جرجه) would be George.

He was one of the Roman generals.

During the fighting, he came to Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and he said: I want to meet you, so they met. Gerja(جرجه) said; I'm gonna ask you in the name of God, and I want you to tell me the truth and don't lie to me.

Because a free man doesn't lie.

They had this chivalry and he is saying to Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد): You are free, man. I'm a free man.

You have to be honest with me, I'll be honest with you.

So he said: I want you to tell me the truth.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) said: I will tell you the truth.

He said: Is it true that your prophet has received a sword from God, and then he gave it to you.

Therefore you never lose in any battle?

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) he could have said: Yes… And built upon that reputation that already existed and carry the legend further and promoted it.

But he didn't. He said: No, that's not true.

What happened is Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ has sent us a prophet, who invited us to the truth.

Some of us believed in him, while some of us fought against him.

I was amongst those who fought against him.

Until Allah سبحانه وتعالى took us by our hearts, gripped our hearts, and brought us forth to Islam, so I became a Muslim.

So, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد), in other words, is saying that we were his enemies, but then Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ gripped our hearts and brought us to Islam.

It was something from the heart we aren't forced into it.

Muhammadﷺ did not force it down on our throats.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ brought our hearts to Him.

Amr Bin Al-Aas رضي الله عنه before he died, he said; There was a time when the most disliked person to me, was Muhammadﷺ and at that time, my greatest desire would be to lay my hands on him and kill him if I could.

But then Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ put the love of Islam in my heart so Muhammadﷺ became the most beloved to me.

And he said: I used to love him so much and have so much respect to him.

I couldn't even look him straight in the eye, I would lower my gaze whenever I see him.

So, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) said: Allah gripped our hearts and we became Muslim.

And then Muhammadﷺ told me; He told me you are a sword among the swords of Allah.

And Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ has drawn you out against the disbelievers.

Thus, I was named the sword of Allah according to that for I am the harshest of the Muslims against the polytheists.

I am the harshest of the Muslims among Al-Mushrikeen(ألمشركين).

So that harshness of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and his skill and his ability and his intelligence, his speed, his willingness to take risk,

is what made Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه, the man he was.

When I talked about the adventure of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) to make Hajj(حَجْ) and then his decision to cross the desert that no one else has crossed before, uncharted territory

that shows you a nature that the majority of the Muslims today have lost.

Muslims have become very timid, they're unwilling to change their ways, the wrong ways.

And they're sort of fixed into a certain course and a certain way of living, and there's no willingness to improve.

And it seems that even the type of work that we're involved in has an effect on our personality.

Definitely work does have an effect on the personality, but the particular line of work of being an employee, where you just do work and then at the end of the month, you receive the fixed salary,

and there's no risk involved that makes a person fear.

So, this I might call it enterprising, or entrepreneurship ability that Sahabah رضي الله عنهم had allowed them to become who they were, by the Taufeeq(توفيق) of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

See, I want to make sure that whenever I talk about the skill of one of a Sahabah رضي الله عنهم we don't attribute their success to that because at the end, it is the Taufeeq(توفيق) of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

See, as a Muslim, you cannot succeed in anything without the Taufeeq(توفيق) of Allah, the Taufeeq(توفيق) of Allah is the willingness of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ and His guidance for you.

So we are not attributing anything to their skills, and that is not something we are supposed to do because with Qaroon(قارون), Qaroon(قارون) and he did not thank Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ for the wealth that Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ has given him.

When he was asked how did you make you wealthy, he said; I made my fortune because of my skills.

He didn't say because Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ gave it to me.

So that's being ungrateful. That is Jaht-In-Neimah(جهت انعمة).

That's rejecting the blessing of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

no Salah(صلاة), no Sayam(صيام), no Zakah(زكوة) nothing, no Zikr(زكر), And Shahadah(شَهَادَة) that's it, you got the higher level in Jannah(جنة).

So the battle started, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) told the right and left flanks to move ahead.

So the retreat was so bad it pushed the Muslim army so far behind that they reached to the fixed basis of the Muslim army.

So the women came out and fought.

Javeria(جويرية), the daughter of Abu Sufiyan(أبوسُفيان) was fighting.

So that was the role that the Muslim women played in the Battle of Al-Yarmook(يرموك).

Muadh Ibn Jabal(معاذإبن جبل), he was encouraging the ones around him.

Abu Sufiyan(أبوسُفيان) was going around one of the Sahabah(صحابه) said; There was a calmness during the fight.

And I went and found Abu Sufiyan(أبوسُفيان) going around his son and encouraging everyone and making Dua(دُعَا) to Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

So they pushed them back to their original locations, and even further back.

So now the tables were turning.

Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه heading a group of Horsemen of about 100 which was very swift and maneuverable.

He decided to make an attack on the left flank of the Roman army.

So he made an attack and it was such a strong blow to the army.

6000 Roman fighters died in that single attack.

So it was such a very strong blow to the left flank of the Army, and then Khalid(خالد) withdraw back and he told his men, he said: In the Name of Allah, they have no patience and strength more than what you have seen.

In other words, we have pushed them to the limit, they can't do any better.

Which means we just need to press a little further, until we push them to the breaking point.

So Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) attacking again and encouraging the Muslims of the right flank under Amr Bin Al-Aas(عَمْرُو بِن اَلْعَاص) to push.

And they succeeded in Tatweek(تطويق), in besieging the Roman army, so just imagine 45,000, besieging 250,000.

So they succeeded in besieging them now, because Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) said, that's the end of it, they cannot fight, they're reaching the breaking point

and Allah Alam(ألله أعلم) how Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه made that judgment.?

Maybe it's by the response that he's seeing from them or the looks on their faces.

He said: Just attack them and surround them.

So they rounded the army from three sides and their back was towards the trench.

Now obviously, there's such a huge army to besiege.

So what Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) then did, He commanded his men to drive a wedge between the cavalry and the infantry, of the Roman army.

So they succeeded in doing that.

So now the cavalry is separated from the infantry.

The horsemen are separate from the foot soldiers.

And then Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) gave his command to Amr Bin Al-Aas(عَمْرُو بِن اَلْعَاص), he told him open an exit door for the cavalry.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) knew that their will, to fight is over, and now they just want to survive.

He knew that they have been pushed to the limit, and that's the end of the resistance.

So he told Amr Bin Al-Aas(عَمْرُو بِن اَلْعَاص) to open up because now they're surrounded from each side.

He told him: Open up, give them a way out, and as soon as Amr Bin Al-Aas(عَمْرُو بِن اَلْعَاص) did that, the cavalry just ran out.

So now you have the foot soldiers without any cover.

And that is when the Muslim army just started pushing them further and further and further.

He said that 80,000 Roman soldiers plunged into the cliff, 80,000.

The total number of losses among the Roman army totaled around 120,000 Soldiers.

80,000 of them in the cliff, they were just falling in numbers, because by now it was nighttime.

And the soldiers are just running away and they don't know what which direction to take.

So some of them are just jumping off the cliff.

Plus, these men, who were chained up their chains ended up killing them.

And that was the prophecy of Amr Bin Al-Aas(عَمْرُو بِن اَلْعَاص), he said; These people have cornered themselves, a cliff and chains, that's all what you need.

And Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) spent his night in the pavilion of Theodore.

Theodore himself was killed.

So now Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) is staying in the tents of the Roman General and the fight is going on at night.

They're just finishing off these soldiers, the ones who are left behind and couldn't run away.

So it was a great victory for the Muslim and that's why the day of Al-Yarmook(يرموك) is such a memorable event in the history of Islam.

Not only because of what happened during the day of Al-Yarmook(يرموك), but because Al-Yarmook(يرموك) was actually the turning point in the Fatoohaat(فتوحات) of Ash-Sham(ألشَّام)

because of what happened during Al-Yarmook(يرموك) the resistance of the Roman Empire in Ash-Sham(ألشَّام) was broken.

And after that, it was just one city falling after another.

And Ash-Sham(ألشَّام) was the gateway to Africa and to Europe.

That is how the Muslims opened Egypt and then North Africa.

So it was a very, very important event.

3000 Muslims died, among them were many Sahabah(صحابه), one of them was Ikrimah Bin Abi Jahal(عكرمة بن أبي جهل).

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) at that time was fighting against the Muslims.

It was Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and Ikrimah(عكرمة), who routed the Muslims and caused the defeat of the Muslims in the battle of Uhud(أحَد).

Ikrimah Bin Abi Jahal(عكرمة بن أبي جهل) was one of the worst enemies of Rasool Allah ﷺ, until Fath-E-Makkah(فتح مكه).

Ikrimah(عكرمة) said: I have fought against Rasool Allah ﷺ, so many times, now on this day shall I retreat.

I have fought against Muhammadﷺ so many times I need to make up for that.

So on this day when Allah is giving me a chance, shall I retreat.

So to ensure that he's going to fight until the last moment, he called upon his close associates and he was ahead of a squadron.

He called upon his close associates, among them, his uncle Al-Haris Bin Hishaam(ألحارث بن هشام), and Ziraar Ibn Azwar(ضرار إبن أزور), and many of the others Sahabah(صحابه) and he said:

Let's give each other a pledge to die Fee-Sabeel-Lillah(فِي سَبيل الله).

In other words, we're gonna throw ourselves plunge into the army of the enemy.

And since we made an oath not to live, we need to stay there until we get Shahadah(شَهَادَة) that's pretty much the Baiyah(بَيْعة) that they gave.

We pledge allegiance to die, we're not going to come back alive.

And this is by the way, one of the evidences, scholars use for the validity of martyrdom operations Amaliyatil Istashhadiyyah(عملية الأستشهادية).

That these Sahabah(صحابه) but not all of them are Sahabah(صحابه) obviously.

Ikrimah(عكرمة) was a Sahabi(صحابي), Al-Haris Bin Hishaam(ألحارث بن هشام) was a Sahabi(صحابي), Ziraar Ibn Azwar(ضرار إبن أزور) was Sahabi(صحابي), the total number of the group was 400, by the way,

this was not a small group 400, they pledged to die.

Why is it used by the scholars as an evidence to support Al-Amaliyatil Istash'hadiyyah(عملية الأستشهادية), it is because of the fact that they promised to die

and to do their best to get Shahadah(شَهَادَة).

The entire group 400, we're laying down on the battleground, so they fulfilled their oath.

Some of them were actually killed and the others were injured so severely that they couldn't move any further.

So they have fulfilled the oath, they did their best.

So the ones, who survived didn't survive because they broke the oath.

They survived because their injuries were so bad, it incapacitated, they couldn't move anymore.

So the water would go to that person, he would say give it to my other brother who needs this more than I do.

So the water would make a full circle and come back to the same person, whom it was offered to before, but by the time most of them are already dead.

Now Ibn Taymiyah(اِبْنِ تَيْمِيَّه) as I mentioned to you before, he said that, The reasoning is that and the wisdom behind that, is that if the Khalifah(خليفه) is very strict,

he has to have somebody under him, who's soft, and if the Khalifah(خليفه) is soft, then he has to have somebody under him who's very strict.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق), and Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) go together very well.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه told Uthman Ibn Affan(عثمان ابن عفان), he told him: If I would bypass, Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) it's not going to get beyond you.

Abu Hurairah(أبوهريرة) said: Because they had work to do, they had businesses, they had farms, but I had nothing and I would accompany Rasool Allah ﷺ on an empty stomach

so one of the young Sahabah(صحابه) went and was witness for Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari(أبوموسى ألأشعري), but the point to make is that that was the personality of Umar(عُمَر).

So Talha(طلحة) said that what will your response be to Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ on the Day of Judgment.

Now Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه said: Because he was laying down, so he wanted them to make him sit, straight.

He said: Are you threatening me by Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.?

If Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ asks me: Why did I appoint Umar(عُمَر)?

I will say because he's the best among us.

Every person in his personality, there are things that you might dislike, but Umar(عُمَر) is the best among you.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه was, he took this comment seriously because he reminded him by Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

So Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) said: This is, what I'll say.

And another narration, If Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ asks me: Why do you appoint Umar(عُمَر) I will say because he is Al-Qawwi(ألقوي), Al-Ameen(ألأمين) he is strong and the trustworthy.

And these were the two words that the daughter of the man in Mad'yan(مدين) used when she went to her father.

After Musa عليه السّلام provided their flock with water.

She went back to her father and said: O my father, why don't you hire that man?

Because the best man to hire is a man, who's strong and trustworthy and that's how Musa(موسى) got a job in Mad'yan(مدين) and he lived there for 10 years.

So this woman or girl at the time, she was very young.

She was very wise in that statements.

So, Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ mentions it in Qur'an that these are the two requirements if you want to hire someone.

This is what you look for, in an interview when you want to hire somebody to work for you.

Is he strong? And strength here doesn't mean necessarily physical strength.

It means competency in that particular field.

So you're strong in the field.

You're competent in that particular field.

If it's a physically demanding work, then the person has to be physically fit.

If it's a mentally demanding work, then the person needs to be mentally fit and strong.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was the perfect person for this role.

He was very intelligent, very wise, very strong, very determined.

He had solid opinions, he can make decisions and he demanded respect from the people around him.

And that's why Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه said: I'm going to appoint him to lead you.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه called Abu Obaidah رضي الله عنه to write down the appointment of Umar(عُمَر), so it was written down.

And then he had it announced in the Masjid(مسجد) and then he had the people give Baiyah(بَيْعة) to Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) while he was still alive.

So the Baiyah(بَيْعة) of Umar(عمر) did not happen, after the death of Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه.

As soon as Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه died Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) immediately assumed his position as Khalifah(خليفه) there was no Baiyah(بَيْعة) that happened after the death, it was already done

and completed before the death of Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه.

The illness of Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) carried on, and his situation was getting worse, until it was the 15th day.

So Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) asked his daughter Ayesha(عائشه), he said: What day did Rasool Allah ﷺ die?

She said: He died on a Monday, Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) said: And this is Monday.

So I think that this will be my last day.

Now this is a very interesting statement.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه was very keen on following Rasool Allah ﷺ his whole Khilafah(خِلَافَه) is an example of followings Sunnah(سنة).

And not just following Sunnah(سنة) in things that don't cost you anything.

He was following Sunnah(سنة) on issues that could cost him and the entire community, their life.

The issue of sending out the army of Osama(أسامة) was not something to be taken light.

That was a very serious risk, and then insisting on having Osama(أسامة) lead the army and not appointing somebody older than him. He was only 18 years old.

And then the fact that he never changed the post of anyone appointed by Rasool Allah ﷺ and make it clear, That I am a man, who will follow and I'm not a man who will innovate.

I'm going to follow Rasool Allah ﷺ and I'm not going to come up with Bid'ah(بدعة).

He was very insistent, and persistent on following the Sunnah(سنة) of Rasool Allah ﷺ to the letter.

And it seems that he even wanted to follow the Sunnah(سنة) of Rasool Allah ﷺ in his death, so he expected that he would die on the same day as Rasool Allah ﷺ died.

And it happened, he died on a Monday and Rasool Allah ﷺ died on a Monday and Rasool Allah ﷺ died at the age of 63 and Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) dies at the age of 63.

So he's following Rasool Allah ﷺ, in his life and in his death.

His last words, in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا) were, My Lord, take me as a Muslim and join me with the righteous, take me as a Muslim and make me join the righteous, make me join my closest friend Muhammadﷺ,

and make me join the Sahabah رضي الله عنه who passed away before.

These were his last words, in Duniyah(دُنِيَّا).

He died the 21st of Jama Al-Aakhirah(جمادالآخِرة) the 13th year of Hijrah(هجرة).

So, his Khilafah(خِلَافَه) was two years, three months and 10 days that was it.

All of these events, battles, Da'wah(دعوة) were done within two years, three months and 10 days.

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab رضي الله عنه had the honor of leading the Salah(صلاة) of Janazah(جنازة) on Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه.

Now when I think about this, the Imam(اِمَام) of Salat-Ul-Janazah(صلاة الجنازة) makes Dua(دُعَا) for the person, who dies.

The Imam(اِمَام) makes a Dua(دُعَا) and everybody behind the Imam(اِمَام) is also making Dua(دُعَا) for the deceased.

So you can imagine Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه covered in the Thaub(ثوب), the cloth, the white cloth, and Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) is the one leading the Salah(صلاة) on him

and he is one making Dua(دُعَا) for Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه, it's Umar(عُمَر) making Dua(دُعَا) for his close friend Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه

asking Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ to grant him the highest level in Jannah(جنة).

And then Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and Uthman Ibn Affan رضي الله عنه and Talha Bin Obaidellah(طلحة بن عبيدالله) and Abdur Rahman Ibn Abi Bakr(عبدالرحمن إبن أبي بكر)

were the ones, who would lower the body of Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه in his grave.

The grave of Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه would be in the room of his daughter Ayesha(عائشه) right next to the grave of Muhammadﷺ.

And out of respect for Muhammadﷺ, the head of Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) was placed at the same level as the shoulders of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

So he's not put right next to him, but he's a little bit behind.

Abdullah Bin Umar(عبدالله بن عمر) he says I came rushing I wanted to enter into the grave and lower the body.

But I came after the body was already lowered and my father told me it's already done.

But the ones, who did that were Umar(عُمَر), Uthman(عثمان), Talha(طلحة) and Abdur Rahman Ibn Abi Bakr رضي الله عنهم أجمعين After two years, three months and 10 days Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه succeeded in.

Number one, establishing the rules of Khilafah(خِلَافَه) in Islam.

Number two, starting the mission of carrying out the Da'wah(دعوة) to the entire world because during the time of Muhammadﷺ, the Da'wah(دعوة) was still within the peninsula.

And the only exception to that was Mu'tah(مَؤتَة) and Tabook(تبوك).

But even with Mu'tah(مَؤتَة) and Tabook(تبوك), even though they were within Roman territory, but it was still populated by Arab tribes in these southern parts of Ash-Sham(ألشَّام),

but it was Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه, who started the mission of Da'wah(دعوة), into the different nations of the world, the Persian people, the Roman people and beyond.

So he was the teacher and the guide of the Mujahideen(مجاهدين) and the Duaah(دعاة) both.

He never had allowed himself the luxury of having spare time.

He never allowed himself the luxury of relaxing and he never allowed himself to benefit financially from his post.

We did talk earlier about the demands of Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) in his salary and even the bargaining.

When he said that this is not enough.

But he was doing it because he had a certain standard of living that he has to take care of himself and his family.

In addition to that he was very generous.

Before he died, since he still had some wealth leftover from his business days, before Khilafah(خِلَافَه) he had pieces of land.

He told his daughter Ayesha(عائشه), I want you to sell my property and then to pay back to the Muslim treasury.

All of the money that I took as a salary when I was Khalifah(خليفه).

I have the money, give it back to the Muslim Treasury.

When Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) heard about that, he said; May Allah have mercy on Abu Bakr(ابوبكر), he's making a difficult on the ones, who will come after him.

He's setting a standard that is too high, he's going to make it difficult on us.

You return all of the money that you have taken from the treasury even though it was Halal(حلال) for you.

You deserve, it was not a deserve, it was less than what he deserves.

He got the money because he had to support a family.

And now since he has money left over, he's gonna pay it back to the Treasury.

So all of what was taken by Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) was returned to Bait-Al-Maal-Al-Muslimeen(بيت المال المسلمين).

مسلمانوں نے چالیس(40) سے پینتالیس(45) ہزار مجاہدین پر مشتمل لشکر تیار کیا جبکہ، ان کے مخالفین کا لشکر تقریباً اڑھائی لاکھ(250,000) جنگجوؤں پر مشتمل تھا

اور ہرقل نے تمام فوج کے سپہ سالار اپنے بھائی تھیوڈر کو خط بھیج کر ایسے میدانِ جنگ کا انتخاب کرنے کو کہا ہرقل نے بھائی سے کہا؛ ایسی جگہ کا انتخاب کرو جو جنگ کے لیے وسیع میدان فراہم کرے لیکن پسپائی اختیار کرنے کی گنجائش نہ ہو

کیونکہ وہ اپنے سپاہیوں کو آخری لمحے تک لڑنے پر مجبور کرنا چاہتا تھا وہ پہلے بھی چند محاذوں پر مسلمانوں سے جنگ سے لڑنے کا تجربہ کر چُکے تھے آپ کے سامنے جنگ موتہ اور پھر اجنادین کا محاز ہے، جو جنگِ یرموک سے پہلے پیش آئے

جس کے متعلق ہم نے پچھلی بار بات کی تھی جس میں حضرت خالد بن ولیدؓ، فلسطین میں حضرت عمرو بن عاصؓ کو بحفاظت نکالنے کے لیے گئے تھے اور انہوں نے رومی فوج کو آ گھیرا اور یہ رومی شہنشاہ کے لیے عبرتناک شکست تھی

چنانچہ اب ہرقل نے ایک بڑا لشکر تیار کیا اور اس نے اپنے بھائی تھیوڈور سے کہا؛ اس بات کو یقینی بناؤ کہ میدانِ جنگ میں پسپا ہونے کی کوئی گُنجائش نہ ہو

تاکہ ہم اپنے فوجیوں کو لڑنے پر مجبور کر سکیں علاوہ ازیں، چٹان کی طرف پشت کئے ہوئے رومی، یرموک کی وادی میں تاحدِ نگاہ پھیلے ہوئے تھے ان کے ساتھ ایسی پیادہ فوج بھی تھی، جوکہ آہنی زنجیروں سے باہم منسلک دس، دس سپاہیوں پر مشتمل دستے تھے

لہذا دس سپاہیوں کے ہر دستے کے پاس ایک آہنی زنجیر تھی، جو انہیں ایک دوسرے سے باندھے ہوئے تھی تاکہ اگر کوئی سپاہی میدان جنگ سے پسپائی اختیار کرنا چاہے تو اسے اپنے پورے دستے کو قائل کرنا پڑے

علاوہ ازیں، اِس وجہ سے ان سپاہیوں کی نقل و حرکت بھی کافی مشکل ہو گئی تھی، لہذا وہ لوگ تقریباً ایک مخصوص انداز سے ہی لڑ سکتے تھے تمام پیادہ سپاہی ایسے نہیں تھے لیکن ان کی کافی بڑی تعداد زنجیروں سے باہمی بندھی ہوئی تھی

اور میرے کہنے کا مطلب یہ ہے کہ یہ جنگی حکمتِ عملی پہلی بار اختیار نہیں کی گئی تھی کیونکہ غزوہ ذات ألسلاسل میں حضرت عمرو بن عاصؓ کو بھی ایسی صورتحال کا سامنا کرنا پڑا تھا

لہذا یہ ایک جنگی حکمتِ عملی تھی جو دراصل ان فوجیوں کو لڑنے پر مجبور کرنے کے لیے استعمال کی گئی تھی تو اب رومیوں نے ہی اس میدانِ جنگ کا انتخاب کیا

اور جب حضرت عمرو بن عاصؓ نے دیکھا تو مسلمانوں سے فرمایا؛ خوش ہوجاؤ کہ یہ فتح کی نوید ہے، شازونادر ہی ایسا ہوتا ہے کہ میدان جنگ میں ایک کونے سے آنے والا حریف فاتح بن جائے

یہ وہ دشمن ہے جس نے جنگ میں اپنے لشکر کے لئے میدانِ جنگ کا ایک کونہ منتخب کیا ہے تو یہ فتح کی نوید ہے، یہ ہمارے لیے نیک شگون ہے رومی فوج منظم دستوں پہ مشتمل تھی جو ان کا جنگ لڑنے کا انداز تھا

جب کہ عرب میں جنگ کرنے کے لئے یہ طریقہ رائج  نہیں تھا لیکن پہلی بار اس جنگی انداز کو یرموک میں استعمال کیا گیا اور حضرت خالد بن ولیدؓ نے اس طرزِ جنگ کو استعمال کرنے کا مشورہ دیا

چنانچہ آپؓ نے اسلامی فوج کو دستوں میں تقسیم کیا، ہر دستہ ایک ہزار سپاہیوں پر مشتمل تھا چنانچہ آپؓ کے لشکر میں چالیس سے پنتالیس دستے تھے اور آپؓ نے ہر دستے کا ایک سپہ سالار مقرر فرمایا

لشکر کا وسطی یا مرکزی حصہ تقریباً اٹھارہ دستوں پہ مشتمل تھا، اس لیے ہم اٹھارہ ہزار فوجیوں کے بارے میں بات کر رہے ہیں اور اس کی قیادت حضرت ابوعبیدہ عمرو بن جراحؓ  کر رہے تھے

جو مستعد و برق رفتار تھے اور ان کی نقل و حرکت بھی دشوار نہیں تھی آپؓ نے ان گھڑسواروں کو آگے، پیچھے دفاعی اور جارحانہ انداز میں متعین کیا آپؓ نے پانچ ہزار سپاہی حضرت سعید بن زیدؓ کی زیرِ قیادت مقرر کئے

اور پانچ ہزار سپاہیوں پر مشتمل اس دستے کا کام دفاع کرنا تھا، اور مسلمان خاندانوں اور ان کی املاک کو دشمن سے محفوظ رکھنا تھا آپ دیکھیں؛ یہ تمام مجاہدین اپنے اہل و عیال، اپنے مال و دولت، سب کچھ لیے فی سبیل اللہ حاضر ہو گئے
